newsitem.title: GERMANY: D.Telekom ordered to revamp some charges.
newsitem.headline: D.Telekom ordered to revamp some charges.

text.p: Germany's Post and Telecommunications Ministry on Friday ordered Deutsche Telekom AG to reorganise the rates it charges for directory services to bring the charges in line with actual costs.

The regulatory intervention marks the first such decision regarding supervision of tariffs under Germany's new telecoms law and was made in response to a complaint by telecoms service group Telegate AG.
Telegate had argued that monopoly Deutsche Telekom was abusing its dominant market position by operating its directory services with rates below costs.
The business daily Handeslblatt newspaper said that while Telekom charges 60 pfennigs per call for directory information, it would have to raise its rates to 1.35 marks to cover costs.
The ministry would not comment on the report and gave no details about prices. Deutsche Telekom also declined to comment.

The ministry added, however, that it could not prevent Telekom from cross-subsidising its directory services because Telekom was required under law to provide these services as part of its universal service duties as dominant carrier.
But the government plans to redefine regulation for standard directory services and would require Telekom to bring its charges in line with costs by January 1, 1998 at the latest.
